covers: Wall Street's Thursday close and after-hours results (Amazon, Intel, Reddit), Asia and commodities overnight, and the SA open on Friday 30 October 2026
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures down 2% as Amazon falls about 7% and Intel about 17–23% after results; Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites push Brent to $115.74 and gold dips below $4,000
summary: In South Africa the rand was at about R16.61 per dollar early on Friday and the JSE Top 40 closed Thursday at 101,875.93 (Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 29–30 Oct), with gold and platinum lower overnight ahead of today's trade and budget balance data. On Wall Street Nasdaq-100 futures were down 2% and S&P 500 futures down 0.8% by 8:47 pm ET after Amazon fell 6.7% after hours on a revenue and profit miss and Intel slumped nearly 23% on weak fourth-quarter guidance (Investing.com, 29 Oct). Brent rose 0.75% to $115.74 after Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities (Reuters via Business Standard, 30 Oct) while spot gold fell 0.7% to $3,992.46 on December Fed-hike bets (Investing.com, 30 Oct) — a mix that tends to support the dollar and weigh on the rand and on richly valued tech shares.

items.title: US futures sink: Nasdaq-100 down 2%, S&P 500 down 0.8% after Amazon and Intel results
items.summary: By 8:47 pm ET on Thursday Nasdaq-100 futures were down 2% at 28,975.0, S&P 500 futures down 0.8% at 7,690.25 and Dow futures up 0.04% at 52,533.0. Amazon fell 6.7% after hours, extending a 4.3% regular-session drop, and Intel slumped nearly 23% after hours; investors also kept bets on a December Fed hike after strong GDP and PCE data (Investing.com, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Amazon misses on sales and profit; Q3 capex $77.3 billion and free cash flow negative $42.4 billion
items.summary: Third-quarter revenue was $201.94 billion (+12%) against $202.31 billion expected and adjusted EPS $1.89 against $1.96; operating income of $28.1 billion beat the $26.2 billion estimate. AWS sales rose 39% to about $45.98 billion, just above forecasts, but online stores ($68.47 billion, +2%) and advertising ($19.64 billion, +11%) missed. Quarterly capex was $77.3 billion against $58.7 billion expected, free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion, and fourth-quarter sales guidance of $240–247 billion has a midpoint below the $244.5 billion consensus; the full-year capex plan stays at $220 billion. Shares fell more than 7% in late trading (SiliconANGLE, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Intel falls about 17% after hours on weak fourth-quarter guidance
items.summary: Intel's third-quarter revenue was $16.5 billion (+21%), in line with estimates, and adjusted EPS $0.52 beat the $0.41 consensus. But it guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15–16 billion against about $17 billion expected and adjusted EPS to $0.25 against $0.43, with gross margin narrowing to 38% from 43%, citing a PC slump expected to last at least through the first half of 2027, high memory prices and supply limits including a 14 October explosion at its Fab 28 plant in Israel. Data centre and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct 2026). Shares fell about 17% after hours (Yahoo Finance) and nearly 23% later in the evening (Investing.com, 29 Oct).

items.title: Houthis say they struck Saudi oil sites; Brent up 0.75% to $115.74, on course for a fourth monthly gain
items.summary: Brent rose 86 cents to $115.74 a barrel and WTI 72 cents to $102.72 at 01:22 GMT on Friday after Yemen's Houthis said they hit Ras Tanura, the Rabigh refinery and an Aramco facility at Abqaiq; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit sea mines near Hormuz. Brent was on course for a gain of nearly 14% in October and WTI about 15%, the fourth straight monthly rise (Reuters via Business Standard, 30 Oct 2026). Higher oil feeds SA fuel prices and inflation.

items.title: Binance hit by a record crypto theft of about $6.3 billion; bitcoin at a six-week low
items.summary: Binance estimated a $6.3 billion impact from a security breach and said about $3 billion had been frozen with partners; Chainalysis put the amount stolen at at least $5.912 billion. Bitcoin fell 3% to $76,469.82, a six-week low, and ether more than 3% to $2,185.83 (Reuters via Investing.com, 29–30 Oct 2026).

items.title: Wall Street closes lower: Nasdaq down 1.38%, S&P 500 down 0.30%, Dow down 0.25%
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,184.73, down 365.13 points or 1.38%; the S&P 500 at 7,720.39, down 23.59 or 0.30%, its first loss in four days; and the Dow at 52,342.56, down 132.54 or 0.25%. Alphabet fell about 13% after its profit miss and negative free cash flow, the main drag on technology shares (Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Alphabet down about 13%, on course for its worst day since its 2004 listing
items.summary: Alphabet shares fell about 13% on Thursday, erasing an estimated $496 billion of market value, the second-largest one-day loss for any US-listed company after Nvidia's roughly $593 billion in January 2025. Third-quarter earnings per share were $2.12 against $3.02 expected, hit by an $8.2 billion unrealised loss mainly on its SpaceX stake; free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion and quarterly capex $51.4 billion (IBTimes, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: US inflation heats up: September PCE 3.6% a year, core 3.1%; markets price an 84.6% chance of a December Fed hike
items.summary: The headline PCE price index rose 0.5% in September and 3.6% from a year earlier (August 3.4%); core PCE rose 0.3% and 3.1% (August 3.0%). Inflation-adjusted consumer spending was flat in September. CME FedWatch showed about an 84.6% probability of a Fed rate hike in December (Reuters via GV Wire, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Reddit falls 8.5% after a soft fourth-quarter outlook
items.summary: Reddit's third-quarter revenue rose 53% to $895 million, above the $874.9 million estimate, and adjusted EPS was $1.40 against $1.33. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $1.00–1.03 billion has a $1.015 billion midpoint, below the $1.05 billion expected; shares fell 8.5% after the report (Investing.com, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: US economy grows 3.4% in the third quarter, faster than the 3.2% expected
items.summary: The first estimate of US GDP showed 3.4% annualised growth in July–September (Convera, 29 Oct 2026), above the 3.2% forecast. Stronger growth alongside elevated inflation supports the dollar and makes a near-term Fed cut less likely; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% on 28 October with two members wanting a hike.

items.title: Microsoft capex $45.2 billion, below the $50.7 billion expected; CoreWeave and Nebius drop
items.summary: Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter capital spending including finance leases was $45.2 billion against a $50.7 billion StreetAccount estimate and its own target of about $50 billion; CFO Amy Hood said some third-party capacity deliveries were delayed. Alphabet's quarterly capex of $51.36 billion was also below the $55.09 billion expected. In overnight trade CoreWeave fell 5.8%, Nebius 6.3%, IREN 5.3% and Applied Digital 4.3% (Stocktwits, 28 Oct).

items.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike
items.summary: The Federal Reserve left its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 October in a 10–2 vote; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a 0.25-point hike (American Banker, 28 Oct). Chair Kevin Warsh gave no guidance on December; the 10-year Treasury yield went back above 5% after his comments before easing, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a December hike at 83.5%, up from 72.8% (Investing.com, 28 Oct). By early Thursday in Asia, traders priced about 78% (Free Malaysia Today, 29 Oct).
items.source: American Banker; AFP via Yahoo News; HousingWire, 28 Oct 2026

items.title: Rand slips to R16.645 as gold and platinum fall; JSE Top 40 edges up 0.1%
items.summary: The rand traded at 16.6450 per dollar at 13:55 GMT, about 0.3% weaker, as gold fell nearly 1% and platinum 2.9%, and after producer inflation rose to 6.2% in September from 5.0% in August. The Top 40 was up 0.1% and the 2035 government bond yield fell 3 basis points to 8.555% in early trade (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: SA economy about 5% bigger after Stats SA rebasing: 2025 GDP now R8.04 trillion
items.summary: Statistics South Africa moved the GDP base year from 2015 to 2022, lifting last year's nominal GDP to R8.04 trillion (about $483 billion) from R7.64 trillion. All 10 sectors were revised up, led by mining, finance and trade, and newly measured activity such as self-generated electricity, illegal mining and e-hailing was added. Economists say a bigger GDP base makes debt-to-GDP and deficit ratios look better; it does not change the debt itself. (Reuters via Investing.com, 29 Oct 2026)

items.title: SA producer inflation jumps to 6.2% in September, above the 5.7% expected
items.summary: Producer price inflation rose to 6.2% year on year in September from 5.0% in August, according to data released on 29 October (FX.co, 29 Oct 2026). Economists polled by Reuters had expected 5.7% (Reuters via Finimize, 29 Oct 2026). Higher factory-gate prices can feed into consumer inflation, which was 4.5% in September; the breakdown by product will be added once verified.

items.title: Money supply and credit growth slow in September
items.summary: M3 money supply growth slowed to 7.93% year on year in September from 8.89% in August, and private-sector credit growth slowed to 6.23% from 7.47%; trade and budget balance data are due Friday (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 29 Oct 2026).

items.title: Moody's: budget update is credit positive; Ba2 rating, positive outlook
items.summary: In a report released on Monday, Moody's said the medium-term budget policy statement was credit positive, citing continued fiscal consolidation despite higher oil prices; the 2026 consolidated deficit target was cut to 3.9% of GDP from 4.0%, helped by a R17.1 billion upward revision to tax revenue. Moody's sees debt at 84.9% of GDP by fiscal 2028, down from about 86.8% in fiscal 2025, but said interest absorbed 18.8% of revenue in fiscal 2025. There was no rating action (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 26 Oct).

items.title: Gold slips below $4,000; platinum down 1.8%
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.7% to $3,992.46 an ounce at about 03:50 GMT on Friday, silver 1.7% to $51.29, platinum 1.8% to $1,460.79 and palladium 1.7% to $989.46, as September's 0.5% monthly PCE rise lifted bets on a Fed hike before year-end. Gold is down more than 3% in October, a second monthly fall (Investing.com, 30 Oct 2026). Weaker gold and platinum weigh on SA miners and the rand.

items.title: Bank of Japan holds at 1.25%, says underlying inflation is in line with 2% for the first time since 2013
items.summary: The BoJ kept its policy rate at 1.25%, the highest since 1995, in an 8–1 vote; Hajime Takata wanted a hike to 1.5%. It said underlying inflation was "generally consistent" with its 2% target; core inflation was 2.1% in September (TokenPost, 30 Oct 2026).

items.title: CME odds of a December Fed hike near 75% after the PCE data
items.summary: After September PCE inflation of 3.6% a year (core 3.1%), CME data put the chance of a December Fed rate hike at about 74.9%, with the Fed funds range at 3.75%–4.00% (TradingKey, 30 Oct 2026); an earlier Reuters reading was 84.6%.

items.title: Europe to release 42 million barrels from emergency oil reserves
items.summary: Europe plans to release 42 million barrels of oil from its reserves over the next three months, a large share of it diesel, to add supply and ease energy costs; Brent was near $114.76 a barrel on Thursday, down about 0.5% on the day (Trading Economics, 29 Oct 2026). A bigger supply cushion would ease pressure on fuel prices, which matters for SA inflation and the rand.

items.title: Dollar steady after the Fed; euro $1.1134, yen ¥158.05
items.summary: The dollar index was at 102.26 early on Thursday in Asia; the euro was down 0.15% at $1.1134 and the dollar up 0.14% at ¥158.045. The dollar slipped after Warsh's press conference, and the 2-year Treasury yield was about 4.71%. The ECB and Bank of Japan are both expected to hold rates (Free Malaysia Today, 29 Oct).

items.title: AMZN: after-hours fall takes Amazon further below its scanner target
items.summary: Amazon closed at $243.79 on 29 October, down 4.2% (LRC Stock Scanner, 29 Oct), already below the $250.70 LRC Stock Scanner target; a fall of about 7% after hours on the revenue and profit miss and heavy capex (SiliconANGLE, 29 Oct) would put it near $227. AMZN is a HOLD; rating unchanged.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 29 Oct 2026; SiliconANGLE, 29 Oct 2026

items.title: INTC: guidance shock takes Intel well below its scanner target
items.summary: Intel closed at $92.07 on 29 October (LRC Stock Scanner), above the $85.88 scanner target that flagged it as overvalued; a 17–23% after-hours fall (Yahoo Finance; Investing.com, 29 Oct) would put it roughly between $71 and $76, below that target. INTC is a HOLD; rating unchanged.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 29 Oct 2026; Yahoo Finance, 29 Oct 2026

items.title: RDDT: after-hours fall leaves Reddit above its scanner target
items.summary: Reddit closed at $129.60 on 29 October (LRC Stock Scanner); an 8.5% fall after the report (Investing.com, 29 Oct) would put it near $119, still above the $104.70 scanner target and below the $142.80 scanner level. RDDT is a HOLD; rating unchanged.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 29 Oct 2026; Investing.com, 29 Oct 2026

items.title: GOOGL, NOW, CAT, LLY: Thursday closes against scanner targets
items.summary: Closes on 29 October (LRC Stock Scanner): Alphabet $283.82 (-12.6%) against a $315.60 target; ServiceNow $109.67 (-27.0%) against $98.96; Caterpillar $647.39 (-9.3%) against $546.30; Eli Lilly $1,373.70 (+6.6%) against $1,068. All four are HOLDs; ratings unchanged.

watch_today: Wall Street open: whether Amazon and Intel's after-hours losses hold and drag the Nasdaq-100 (futures -2%)
SA trade balance and budget balance data today; rand near R16.61
Brent near $116 after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites; any Iran response to US outreach
Gold around $4,000 and platinum near $1,460 — pressure on JSE miners
Binance hack fallout and crypto prices; month-end flows on the last trading day of October
